items.title: 'A lot of stigma': The 'taboo' cancer side effects we don't talk about
items.description: Shame and stigma mean gynaecological side effects from cancer treatment — affecting women's sexual, urinary and reproductive health — are under-reported and under-researched.

items.title: China warns Australia over landmark military alliance in the Pacific
items.description: China has warned Australia not to harm its interests in the Pacific after Anthony Albanese struck a landmark military alliance with Fiji.

items.title: Live: Chinese missile test appeared to land near Nauru, Taiwan says
items.description: The nuclear-capable missile test, which China fired into the Pacific yesterday, appears to have landed near the exclusive economic zones of Pacific nations Nauru and Tuvalu. Follow live.

items.title: Donald Trump teaches crypto devotees a valuable lesson
items.description: US President Donald Trump should have been a godsend to the mysterious world of cryptocurrency. Instead, it has been a godsend to him.

items.title: One in every class: AI-assisted sexual abuse widespread among teens
items.description: About one in every 25 Australians under the age of 18 has been the victim or knows a victim of artificial intelligence-assisted online sexual abuse, according to a new study.

items.title: Live: 'Pathetic' Portugal coach slammed for 'scandalous' coaching after Spain defeat
items.description: Spain's Mikel Merino scores in injury time to snatch a 1-0 win over Portugal in a cagey affair in Dallas. Follow live.

items.title: Families told accused Bali bomber Hambali to face 202 life terms
items.description: US military prosecutors reveal new details about their case against the man accused of planning the 2002 Bali bombings, telling the loved ones of Australian victims his trial could finally begin next year.

items.title: Hamas to dissolve emergency government in Gaza
items.description: Hamas officials announced the resignation of senior members of the government, but warned that some people would remain in senior positions in Gaza's administration to "prevent any vacuum that could harm our citizens".

items.title: Pam the Bird graffiti vandal stuck up bridge in standoff with police
items.description: A trespasser remains attached to a 140-metre-tall tower of the Bolte Bridge in Melbourne after spray-painting the surface with the notorious graffiti symbol.

items.title: 'Bad blood' between US and European allies as NATO summit begins
items.description: Dozens of world leaders are descending on Türkiye this week to rubber-stamp significant NATO commitments, but the dynamics on the sidelines could prove more interesting to watch.

items.title: 'Disappointing': Prince Harry and king's awkward stand-off over palace
items.description: The strained relationship between Prince Harry and his father, King Charles III, has been laid bare once again, after an awkward stand-off over accommodation at Buckingham Palace.

items.title: The 'walking archive' helping First Nations people discover family history
items.description: For 28 years, Ali Abdullah-Highfold has helped thousands of Indigenous people find familial connections through his work at the South Australian Museum.

items.title: WorkSafe investigates after footballer suffers life-ending head injuries
items.description: Victoria's workplace safety watchdog is investigating after a suburban footy player was injured, and later died, after his head collided with a cricket pitch.

items.title: Alex de Minaur suffers another 'truly gut-wrenching' Wimbledon loss
items.description: Alex de Minaur loses in the fourth round at Wimbledon in another match he feels he could, and maybe should, have won against ninth seed Flavio Cobolli.

items.title: Too cold to exercise? Here’s how to start and stay on track
items.description: Experts say winter is a good time to double down on exercise rather than taking the foot off the gas.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Your challenge in today's ABC Places quiz is to work out the location of 10 photos from around the world. Be warned: we might try to trick you.

items.title: Cancel your subscriptions: Here are the films and TV you can watch free
items.description: From Bluey in Yolŋu Matha to the first feature film directed by an Indigenous woman, there is a trove of free movies and TV to dive into this NAIDOC Week.

items.title: Sudden venue closures a 'big blow' for Hobart but not unexpected
items.description: There are questions around the future of Hobart's nightlife after the abrupt closure of some of the capital city's most loved institutions due to challenging trading conditions.

items.title: Man with DV convictions cleared to work with children as church minister
items.description: The man's case is one of the last appeals filed in the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal before the law changed in September last year.

items.title: 'Longstanding injustice': Doubts cast over guilt for three of 'Croatian Six'
items.description: An inquiry has raised "reasonable doubt" over the guilt of three of six Croatian men jailed in 1981 over an alleged terrorist plot to bomb several Sydney buildings in 1979.

items.title: Queensland mental health services face funding 'shortfall'
items.description: Queensland mental health community services receive funding from government departments based on an indexation rate.

items.title: Man behind a bold CBD plan may have been running insolvent companies
items.description: The Tasmanian government and a local council welcomed a bold plan to transform Launceston’s CBD from a man who may have been running insolvent companies at the time, an investigation shows.

items.title: What you need to know before claiming your phone as a tax deduction
items.description: The cost of buying and using your own phone may be tax deductible, but the ATO has specific rules about how employees calculate these expenses.

items.title: Australia urged to sign treaty banning nuclear weapons
items.description: There are renewed calls for Australia to sign a treaty ensuring nuclear weapons can't ever be facilitated, stored or manufactured in Australia.

items.title: Germany cracks down on 'extraordinary' rate of sick leave
items.description: Chucking a sickie is no longer as easy as a quick phone call in Germany, under new laws hoped to boost productivity. Here's how the world is responding.
